benchmark_gaps: No throughput benchmarks for EventBus publish/subscribe — no events/sec measurement under varying subscriber counts
No latency benchmarks for sync vs async publish paths — publish_async vs publish not compared
No benchmark for FileEventStore append throughput or replay latency as file grows
No benchmark for FarmState serialization/deserialization throughput (to_dict/from_dict, to_json/from_json)
No benchmark for FarmStateHistory append and query performance at max_size boundary
No benchmark for UnifiedOptimizer solve latency across solver types (TSP, VRP, GPU_TSP, GPU_VRP)
No benchmark for UnionFind operations at scale (10K+ elements, deep chains)
No benchmark for event bus with persistence enabled vs in-memory only
No stress test for event bus under burst load (1000+ events in rapid succession)
No benchmark for schema validation overhead on publish path
No benchmark for exactly-once deduplication memory growth over time
No benchmark for dead letter queue accumulation rate
bottlenecks: Synchronous handler invocation blocks publishers — a slow handler stalls all subsequent handlers and the publisher thread
No backpressure or flow control — publish() accepts events unconditionally, risking memory exhaustion under burst load
FileEventStore.append() opens and closes the file on every event — no write buffering, causing excessive I/O syscalls
FileEventStore lacks fsync — crash can lose last event or corrupt JSONL file
No event store rotation or compaction — FileEventStore grows unbounded, slowing replay and consuming disk
Exactly-once deduplication uses in-memory set only — lost on restart, violating delivery guarantee after recovery
No handler timeout — a hung handler blocks the entire publish() call indefinitely
Dead letter queue is terminal — no retry, replay, or depth alerting mechanism
No event ordering guarantees across types — no global sequence number for causal reconstruction
No wildcard or pattern-based subscriptions — subscribers must know exact event type strings, causing tight coupling
No event filtering by source or payload — subscribers receive all events of a type, wasting handler invocations
No metrics or observability hooks — no counters, latency histograms, or monitoring export
No graceful shutdown or drain — events lost during application shutdown
FarmState.to_dict() excludes tenant_id — multi-tenant deployments lose tenant context on serialization
No cross-field validation rules — only per-field range checks, missing relational constraints (e.g., high temp + low moisture = stress)
No concurrency control for FarmState updates — no locking or compare-and-swap, risking lost-update race conditions
UnifiedOptimizer.solve() is synchronous — large problems block caller with no progress callbacks or cancellation
No result caching in UnifiedOptimizer — identical problems re-solved from scratch
No timeout handling on solve() — pathological problems can run indefinitely
No fallback solver on failure — single point of failure with no graceful degradation
UnifiedOptimizer does not validate problem before solving — errors surface deep in solver internals
No solver auto-selection heuristics — caller must specify solver_type explicitly
FarmState has no integration with event bus — state changes do not automatically publish events
No transition history or audit log in StateTransitionValidator — cannot reconstruct why state changed
No formal state machine pattern — transitions validated by ad-hoc rules, not explicit state graph
missing_algorithms: No circuit breaker pattern for failing handlers — repeated failures do not trip a circuit to skip the handler
No bulkhead isolation between event types — one slow event type can starve others sharing the same bus
No event batching or windowing — handlers are invoked per-event with no micro-batching support
No consistent hashing or partitioning for event distribution across multiple bus instances
No vector clock or logical clock implementation for cross-module causal ordering
No CRDT-based state merge for FarmState — concurrent updates from multiple sources cannot be automatically reconciled
No sliding window rate limiter for event publishing — no token bucket or leaky bucket algorithm
No exponential backoff with jitter for retry — current retry uses fixed exponential backoff without jitter, risking thundering herd
No LRU or LFU cache for UnifiedOptimizer result memoization
No priority queue for event processing — all events processed in FIFO order regardless of urgency
No topological sort for event dependency resolution — events with ordering constraints cannot be sequenced
No Bloom filter for exactly-once deduplication — current in-memory set does not scale and is lost on restart
No Merkle tree or checksum-based integrity verification for FileEventStore — corruption detection is absent
No Raft or Paxos consensus for event bus replication — single-node bus has no HA failover
No greedy set cover or knapsack algorithm for sensor placement optimization in integration context
No A* or Dijkstra pathfinding in integration layer — path planning is isolated from event bus
No Hungarian algorithm or min-cost max-flow in integration layer — task allocation is isolated
No Monte Carlo tree search or simulated annealing wrapper in UnifiedOptimizer — only TSP/VRP solvers exposed
No multi-objective optimization (Pareto frontier) support — only single-objective cost minimization
No VRPTW (VRP with time windows) solver — real-world routing often requires delivery time windows
No column generation or branch-and-bound wrapper for large-scale routing problems
No online/incremental solver interface — cannot add customers or constraints to an existing solution efficiently
No constraint programming (CP) or SAT solver integration for complex scheduling constraints
